attributes.name: applicable_equipment_class
attributes.description: Equipment class or asset type classification code for which this job plan is applicable (e.g., CNC-LATHE, ROBOT-WELDING, CONVEYOR-BELT, COMPRESSOR-SCREW). Enables automatic job plan assignment when creating PM schedules for assets of a given class.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the maintenance engineer or supervisor who formally approved this job plan for operational use. Required for ISO 9001 document control and change management compliance.

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which this job plan was formally approved for use. Supports document control, audit trails, and compliance reporting per ISO 9001 requirements.

attributes.name: asset_category
attributes.description: Category of physical asset or equipment type this job plan is designed for (e.g., CNC Machine, PLC Panel, Conveyor System, Hydraulic Press, HVAC Unit, Robotic Arm). Enables filtering and reuse of job plans across similar asset classes.

attributes.name: confined_space_entry
attributes.description: Indicates whether this job plan involves entry into a permit-required confined space as defined by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146. Triggers additional safety controls, atmospheric testing, and standby attendant requirements.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this job plan record was first created in the source system. Provides audit trail for record creation and supports data lineage in the lakehouse silver layer.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all cost estimates in this job plan (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Ensures consistent financial reporting across multi-site operations.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the maintenance procedure, scope of work, and objectives covered by this job plan. Provides context for planners and technicians beyond the short title.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this job plan version becomes effective and can be applied to work orders and PM schedules. Supports version management and ensures only current approved procedures are used.

attributes.name: estimated_downtime_hours
attributes.description: Estimated production downtime in hours required to execute this job plan. Used for production scheduling, OEE impact analysis, and maintenance window planning. Distinct from labor duration as it represents asset unavailability time.

attributes.name: estimated_duration_hours
attributes.description: Total estimated labor hours required to complete all task steps in this job plan. Used for work order scheduling, capacity planning, and maintenance cost estimation. Represents the sum of all task step estimated hours.

attributes.name: estimated_labor_cost
attributes.description: Estimated total labor cost to execute this job plan, calculated from craft rates and estimated hours. Used for maintenance budget planning and CapEx/OpEx analysis. Expressed in the operational currency.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which this job plan version expires and must be reviewed or replaced. Null for open-ended plans. Supports periodic review cycles mandated by ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 document control requirements.

attributes.name: frequency_interval
attributes.description: Numeric interval value for scheduling this job plan on PM schedules. Interpreted in conjunction with frequency_unit (e.g., interval=3 with unit=MONTH means every 3 months). Null for condition-based or on-demand plans.

attributes.name: frequency_type
attributes.description: Defines the trigger basis for scheduling this job plan on PM schedules. TIME_BASED = calendar interval; METER_BASED = usage/runtime meter (hours, cycles, km); CONDITION_BASED = triggered by condition monitoring threshold; EVENT_BASED = triggered by a specific event; ON_DEMAND = unscheduled/corrective.

attributes.name: frequency_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the maintenance frequency interval. Defines whether the interval is time-based (DAY, WEEK, MONTH, YEAR), meter-based (HOUR, CYCLE, KM, RUNTIME_HOUR), or other. Used with frequency_interval to compute PM due dates. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HOUR|DAY|WEEK|MONTH|YEAR|CYCLE|KM|RUNTIME_HOUR — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: hazardous_materials_involved
attributes.description: Indicates whether the execution of this job plan involves handling, exposure to, or disposal of hazardous materials (chemicals, lubricants, refrigerants, etc.). Triggers environmental compliance controls per EPA and ISO 14001 requirements.

attributes.name: inspection_checklist_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the associated inspection checklist or measurement point document linked to this job plan. Used when the job plan includes condition monitoring readings, SPC measurement points, or quality inspection steps.

attributes.name: job_plan_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the job plan as assigned in Maximo or SAP PM Task List. Used by maintenance planners and technicians to reference the standard procedure (e.g., JP-MECH-0042, TASKLIST-PM-001).

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: Date on which this job plan was last formally reviewed for accuracy, safety compliance, and alignment with current OEM recommendations. Supports periodic review tracking per ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 document control.

attributes.name: loto_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) energy isolation procedures are mandatory before executing this job plan. Drives safety compliance workflows and permit-to-work issuance in the CMMS.

attributes.name: manufacturer_reference
attributes.description: Manufacturer name or OEM reference associated with this job plan, indicating the equipment manufacturer whose maintenance recommendations informed this procedure (e.g., Siemens, Fanuc, ABB, Bosch Rexroth). Supports OEM-aligned maintenance compliance.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this job plan record was last modified in the source system. Supports change tracking, audit trails, and incremental data loading in the lakehouse silver layer.

attributes.name: oem_procedure_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or document identifier from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) maintenance manual or service bulletin that this job plan is based on or aligned with. Ensures traceability to manufacturer-recommended procedures.

attributes.name: permit_to_work_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal Permit to Work (PTW) must be issued and approved before this job plan can be executed. Applies to high-risk activities such as hot work, confined space entry, and electrical work on live systems.

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the job plan indicating whether it is available for use on work orders and PM schedules. DRAFT = under development; ACTIVE = approved and in use; INACTIVE = temporarily suspended; PENDING_REVIEW = awaiting approval; OBSOLETE = superseded and retired.

attributes.name: plan_type
attributes.description: Classification of the maintenance activity type this job plan covers. Drives scheduling logic, resource allocation, and KPI reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PREVENTIVE|CORRECTIVE|PREDICTIVE|INSPECTION|OVERHAUL|LUBRICATION|CALIBRATION|EMERGENCY|SHUTDOWN — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: planner_group
attributes.description: Maintenance planner group or planning team responsible for maintaining and executing this job plan (e.g., MECH-PLANNER-01, ELEC-PLANNER-NORTH). Aligns with SAP PM Planner Group and Maximo planning organization structure.

attributes.name: ppe_requirements
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or narrative description of required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for executing this job plan (e.g., safety glasses, hard hat, arc flash suit, chemical gloves, hearing protection). Mandatory for ISO 45001 and OSHA compliance.

attributes.name: primary_craft
attributes.description: The primary labor craft or trade skill required to execute this job plan (e.g., Millwright, Electrician, Instrumentation Technician, Mechanic). Sourced from Maximo Craft master and used for work order labor planning.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Default priority level assigned to work orders generated from this job plan. Drives scheduling urgency and resource allocation in the CMMS. CRITICAL = safety/production-critical; HIGH = significant impact; MEDIUM = moderate impact; LOW = minor impact; ROUTINE = standard scheduled.

attributes.name: regulatory_compliance_ref
attributes.description: Reference to applicable regulatory standards, codes, or compliance requirements that this job plan satisfies (e.g., ISO 9001, ISO 45001, OSHA 1910.147, IEC 62443, UL certification requirement). Supports compliance audit traceability.

attributes.name: required_technician_count
attributes.description: Minimum number of technicians required to safely and effectively execute this job plan. Used for crew scheduling and compliance with safety regulations (e.g., confined space entry requiring a standby person per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146).

attributes.name: required_tools
attributes.description: List of specialized tools, equipment, and instruments required to execute this job plan (e.g., torque wrench, vibration analyzer, multimeter, alignment laser, hydraulic jack). Used for tool reservation and kitting in the CMMS.

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: Version or revision identifier of the job plan, incremented each time the procedure is formally updated (e.g., REV-01, REV-02). Supports change control and audit traceability per ISO 9001 document control requirements.

attributes.name: safety_precautions
attributes.description: Narrative description of mandatory safety precautions, lockout/tagout (LOTO) requirements, personal protective equipment (PPE), and hazard controls that must be observed before and during execution of this job plan. Compliance with OSHA and ISO 45001 requirements.

attributes.name: shutdown_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether execution of this job plan requires a planned production shutdown or equipment isolation. Used for maintenance window scheduling and production planning coordination to minimize OEE impact.

attributes.name: site_code
attributes.description: Plant or facility site code where this job plan is applicable. Enables site-specific job plan management in multi-site manufacturing operations. Aligns with SAP Plant code and Maximo Site.

attributes.name: source_system_key
attributes.description: Natural key or identifier of this job plan record in the originating source system (e.g., Maximo Job Plan Number, SAP PM Task List Number). Enables traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse and operational systems.

attributes.name: spare_parts_list
attributes.description: Narrative or structured list of spare parts and materials required for this job plan, including part numbers and quantities (e.g., 'Bearing SKF 6205-2RS x2, O-Ring Kit x1, Filter Element x1'). Used for pre-kitting and MRP-driven spare parts reservation.

attributes.name: task_step_count
attributes.description: Total number of discrete task steps defined within this job plan. Provides a quick indicator of procedure complexity and is used for work order progress tracking in Maximo and Siemens Opcenter MES.

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive title of the job plan summarizing the maintenance activity (e.g., 'Annual Preventive Maintenance - CNC Spindle Assembly', 'Hydraulic System Inspection'). Used in work order templates and PM schedules.

attributes.name: work_category
attributes.description: Trade or discipline category of the maintenance work defined in this job plan. Used to route work orders to the correct craft group and for workforce planning. attributes.name: work_order_type
attributes.description: Default work order type that should be generated when this job plan is applied. PM = Preventive Maintenance; CM = Corrective Maintenance; EM = Emergency Maintenance; INSPECTION = Inspection only; OVERHAUL = Major overhaul; PROJECT = Capital project work.

products.name: failure_record
products.description: Failure event record capturing equipment breakdowns and fault occurrences, including failure date/time, failure class, failure mode code, failure cause code, remedy code, affected component, downtime start/end, production impact (units lost), and MTBF contribution data. Embeds the full failure mode classification taxonomy: failure mode description, affected component class, potential cause, detection method, severity rating, occurrence rating, detection rating, and RPN (Risk Priority Number) derived from FMEA/PFMEA analysis. Serves as both the transactional failure event record and the reference catalog for standardized failure modes per equipment class. Feeds MTBF/MTTR reliability analysis, FMEA validation, and maintenance strategy selection. Sourced from Maximo Failure Reporting and SAP PM Notifications.

attributes.name: asset_operating_hours_at_failure

attributes.name: capa_reference_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Reference Number
attributes.description: The reference number of the formal CAPA record initiated in response to this failure event. Populated when capa_required_flag is True. Enables traceability between the failure event and the quality management corrective action process.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this failure record was first created in the system of record. Serves as the audit creation timestamp, distinct from the actual failure event time. Used for data lineage and audit trail compliance.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the repair_cost amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Supports multi-currency operations across global manufacturing sites.

attributes.name: detection_method_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating how the failure was detected (e.g., operator observation, automated alarm, predictive sensor alert, scheduled inspection, SCADA alarm, condition monitoring). Sourced from FMEA detection method taxonomy and Aveva SCADA alarm data. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: operator_observation|scada_alarm|condition_monitoring|scheduled_inspection|predictive_alert|customer_report|automated_sensor — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: detection_rating
attributes.description: Numeric detection rating (1-10 scale) from the FMEA/PFMEA analysis indicating the ability of current controls to detect the failure cause or mode before it reaches the customer or causes production impact. A rating of 10 represents the lowest detectability. Used in RPN calculation.

attributes.name: downtime_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of equipment downtime in minutes resulting from this failure event, calculated as the difference between downtime_end_datetime and downtime_start_datetime. Stored as a business-captured field from the source system (Maximo) rather than derived at query time. Feeds OEE, MTTR, and production impact analysis.

attributes.name: downtime_end_datetime
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the equipment was restored to operational status following the failure event. Used in conjunction with downtime_start_datetime to calculate total downtime duration and MTTR. Null if equipment has not yet been restored.

attributes.name: downtime_start_datetime
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the equipment became unavailable for production due to this failure event. Used to calculate total downtime duration and OEE impact. Feeds MTTR analysis and production loss quantification.

attributes.name: environmental_incident_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this failure event resulted in an environmental incident such as a spill, emission exceedance, or hazardous material release. True if an environmental event occurred; False otherwise. Triggers EPA and ISO 14001 reporting obligations.

attributes.name: failure_cause_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the root cause of the failure event (e.g., inadequate lubrication, overload, material defect, operator error, design deficiency). Sourced from the Maximo Failure Cause catalog and used in CAPA and FMEA root cause analysis.

attributes.name: failure_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the identified root cause of the failure, providing narrative context for the failure_cause_code. Supports CAPA documentation and FMEA validation.

attributes.name: failure_class_code
attributes.description: Standardized classification code categorizing the type of failure at the highest level of the failure taxonomy (e.g., mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, software, structural). Sourced from the Maximo Failure Class hierarchy and aligned with ISO 14224 failure classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mechanical|electrical|hydraulic|pneumatic|software|structural|thermal|instrumentation|process — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: failure_class_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the failure class, providing context for the failure_class_code. Used in maintenance reports, FMEA documentation, and reliability dashboards.

attributes.name: failure_datetime
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the equipment failure or fault was detected or reported. This is the principal real-world event timestamp for the failure record, distinct from the record creation audit timestamp. Used as the anchor for MTBF calculations and downtime duration derivation.

attributes.name: failure_impact_type
attributes.description: Classification of the operational impact of the failure event on production and safety. 'production_stoppage' indicates complete halt of production; 'partial_degradation' indicates reduced throughput or capacity; 'quality_impact' indicates output quality was affected; 'safety_incident' indicates a safety hazard was created; 'no_production_impact' indicates the failure was detected without affecting output.

attributes.name: failure_mode_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the specific manner in which the equipment failed (e.g., wear, fracture, corrosion, overheating, short circuit, vibration). Sourced from the Maximo Failure Mode catalog and aligned with FMEA/PFMEA failure mode taxonomy. Feeds FMEA validation and maintenance strategy selection.

attributes.name: failure_mode_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the failure mode, explaining how the equipment deviated from its intended function. Embedded from the FMEA/PFMEA failure mode classification taxonomy. Used in reliability analysis and maintenance strategy documentation.

attributes.name: failure_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description of the failure event as recorded by the reporting technician or operator. Captures contextual details not covered by structured codes, including observed symptoms, environmental conditions, and sequence of events. Used in root cause analysis and knowledge base enrichment.

attributes.name: failure_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable business identifier for this failure event record. Used in maintenance reports, CAPA documentation, and cross-system references. Follows the format FR-XXXXXXXXXX.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this failure record was most recently modified. Tracks the latest update for change management, audit compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing.

attributes.name: maintenance_type
attributes.description: Classification of the maintenance response triggered by this failure event. 'corrective' indicates planned corrective maintenance; 'emergency' indicates unplanned breakdown response; 'predictive' indicates maintenance triggered by condition monitoring prediction; 'preventive' indicates a failure discovered during scheduled PM; 'condition_based' indicates maintenance triggered by condition threshold breach.

attributes.name: mtbf_contribution_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) Contribution Hours
attributes.description: The operating hours accumulated on the asset since the previous failure event of the same failure class, contributing to the MTBF calculation for this asset and failure class combination. Stored as a raw business input value from Maximo rather than an aggregated metric. Feeds reliability analysis and TPM strategy.

tag_set.value: Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) Contribution Hours

attributes.name: ncr_reference_number

attributes.name: occurrence_rating
attributes.description: Numeric occurrence rating (1-10 scale) from the FMEA/PFMEA analysis indicating the likelihood or frequency of the failure cause occurring. A rating of 10 represents the highest probability of occurrence. Used in RPN calculation and preventive maintenance scheduling.

attributes.name: plant_code
attributes.description: SAP plant code identifying the manufacturing facility or site where the failure event occurred. Enables geographic and site-level failure analysis and supports multi-plant reliability benchmarking.

attributes.name: potential_failure_effect
attributes.description: Description of the potential effect or consequence of the failure mode on the process, product quality, equipment, or safety. Embedded from the FMEA failure mode classification taxonomy. Used in FMEA validation and maintenance strategy documentation.

attributes.name: production_units_lost
attributes.description: Estimated number of production units (parts, assemblies, or output units) lost due to this failure event and associated downtime. Quantifies the direct production impact for OEE performance loss analysis and financial impact assessment.

attributes.name: record_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the failure record workflow. 'open' indicates the failure has been reported but not yet actioned; 'in_progress' indicates active remediation; 'closed' indicates the failure has been resolved and verified; 'cancelled' indicates the record was voided; 'pending_review' indicates awaiting quality or engineering sign-off.

attributes.name: remedy_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the corrective action or remedy applied to resolve the failure (e.g., replacement, repair, adjustment, cleaning, lubrication, recalibration). Sourced from the Maximo Remedy catalog and SAP PM catalog codes.

attributes.name: remedy_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the corrective action taken to resolve the failure event. Provides narrative context for the remedy_code and supports maintenance knowledge base and CAPA documentation.

attributes.name: repair_cost
attributes.description: Total cost incurred to remediate this failure event, including labor, spare parts, and external contractor costs. Expressed in the local operating currency. Used for maintenance cost analysis, CapEx vs OpEx classification, and total cost of ownership (TCO) reporting.

attributes.name: risk_priority_number
attributes.description: Risk Priority Number derived from FMEA/PFMEA analysis, calculated as the product of severity_rating × occurrence_rating × detection_rating (range 1-1000). Stored as a business-captured value from the FMEA source record rather than computed at query time. Used to prioritize corrective actions and maintenance strategy selection.

attributes.name: safety_incident_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this failure event resulted in or contributed to a safety incident, near-miss, or occupational hazard. True if a safety event occurred; False otherwise. Triggers mandatory OSHA/ISO 45001 reporting workflows and CAPA initiation.

attributes.name: severity_rating
attributes.description: Numeric severity rating (1-10 scale) from the FMEA/PFMEA analysis indicating the seriousness of the failure effect on the product, process, or safety. A rating of 10 represents the most severe impact (safety hazard or regulatory non-compliance). Used in RPN calculation and maintenance strategy prioritization.

attributes.name: spare_part_consumed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more spare parts were consumed during the remediation of this failure event. True if spare parts were used; False otherwise. Feeds spare parts inventory consumption analysis and reorder planning.

attributes.description: Method by which the downtime event was detected and captured. Distinguishes automated detection (SCADA alarm, MES alert, IIoT sensor trigger, predictive maintenance alert) from manual detection (operator report, visual inspection, manual entry). Supports data quality assessment and IIoT maturity tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scada_alarm|mes_alert|operator_report|sensor_trigger|visual_inspection|predictive_alert|manual_entry — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: downtime_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the downtime event type. Drives OEE availability loss categorization and Pareto analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: breakdown|planned_maintenance|changeover|tooling|material_shortage|quality_hold|no_operator|utility_failure|scheduled_break|trial_run — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: downtime_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the downtime event was unplanned (unexpected equipment failure, breakdown) or planned (scheduled maintenance, changeover, tooling change). Critical discriminator for OEE availability calculation — only unplanned downtime reduces OEE availability.

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total elapsed duration of the downtime event in minutes, calculated as the difference between end_timestamp and start_timestamp. Stored as a business field for direct use in OEE availability calculations, Pareto analysis, and production loss costing. Null if event is still open.

attributes.name: end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the equipment was restored to operational status and production resumed. Null if the event is still open/in-progress. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: environmental_impact_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this downtime event resulted in an environmental impact (e.g., spill, emission exceedance, energy waste) requiring EPA or ISO 14001 reporting. True = environmental impact occurred.

attributes.name: estimated_loss_cost
attributes.description: Estimated financial cost of production loss attributable to this downtime event, expressed in the plant's local currency. Calculated from estimated_production_loss_units multiplied by the standard cost per unit. Used for downtime Pareto cost analysis and CapEx justification.

attributes.name: estimated_production_loss_units
attributes.description: Estimated number of production units lost due to this downtime event, calculated based on the equipment's standard throughput rate and the downtime duration. Used for production loss costing and OEE throughput impact analysis.

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the downtime event (e.g., DT-2024-000123). Used for cross-system reference, operator communication, and audit trail. Sourced from Maximo or Siemens Opcenter MES downtime capture.

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the downtime event record. 'open' indicates the stoppage is active; 'in_progress' indicates maintenance is underway; 'resolved' indicates equipment is restored; 'closed' indicates the record is fully documented and approved; 'cancelled' indicates a false or erroneous entry.

attributes.name: failure_class
attributes.description: High-level classification of the failure mode grouping (mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, software, instrumentation, structural, operator_error, external). Aligns with Maximo failure class hierarchy and supports FMEA/PFMEA analysis and spare parts categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mechanical|electrical|hydraulic|pneumatic|software|instrumentation|structural|operator_error|external — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: failure_code
attributes.description: Maximo/CMMS standardized failure code classifying the type of equipment failure (e.g., bearing failure, seal leak, motor burnout, software fault). Distinct from root_cause_code — failure_code describes WHAT failed, root_cause_code describes WHY. Used for MTBF analysis and spare parts planning.

attributes.name: is_repeat_failure
attributes.description: Indicates whether this downtime event is a recurrence of a previously recorded failure on the same asset within a defined lookback period (typically 30 or 90 days). True = repeat failure. Used to trigger CAPA escalation and identify chronic equipment issues.

attributes.name: is_safety_incident
attributes.description: Indicates whether this downtime event was associated with or caused a safety incident (True) or not (False). Triggers mandatory safety reporting workflows and OSHA recordkeeping requirements when True.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the downtime event record (e.g., root cause update, closure, CAPA linkage). Supports change tracking and data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: maintenance_type
attributes.description: Classification of the maintenance activity associated with this downtime event. Distinguishes corrective (reactive repair), preventive (scheduled PM), predictive (condition-triggered), condition-based, and emergency maintenance. Supports TPM and maintenance strategy analysis.

attributes.name: ncr_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the Non-Conformance Report (NCR) associated with this downtime event, applicable when the stoppage was caused by or resulted in a quality non-conformance (e.g., quality hold, defective material). Links downtime to quality management records.

attributes.name: oee_availability_impact_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) Availability Impact Percentage
attributes.description: The percentage reduction in OEE availability attributable to this specific downtime event, expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 4.17 = 4.17%). Calculated as (duration_minutes / planned_production_time_minutes) * 100 for the affected shift/period. Feeds OEE calculation pipelines.

tag_set.value: Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) Availability Impact Percentage

attributes.name: plc_fault_code
attributes.description: The fault or error code reported by the Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) or DCS at the time of the downtime event. Provides low-level diagnostic information for maintenance engineers and supports automated fault classification.

attributes.name: problem_code
attributes.description: Maximo CMMS problem code describing the observed symptom or problem that triggered the downtime event (e.g., vibration, overheating, noise, no output). Part of the Maximo failure reporting triad: problem_code → failure_code → root_cause_code.

attributes.name: remedy_code
attributes.description: Maximo CMMS remedy code describing the corrective action taken to restore the equipment (e.g., replaced bearing, adjusted alignment, reset PLC, cleaned filter). Completes the Maximo failure reporting triad and supports maintenance knowledge base and CAPA closure.

attributes.name: repair_time_minutes
attributes.description: Elapsed time in minutes from when maintenance work began to when the equipment was restored to operational status. Core component of Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) calculation. Excludes waiting/response time.

attributes.name: response_time_minutes
attributes.description: Elapsed time in minutes from the downtime event start_timestamp to when a maintenance technician acknowledged or began working on the issue. Component of Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) analysis and maintenance SLA performance tracking.

attributes.name: root_cause_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the root cause of the downtime event (e.g., mechanical failure, electrical fault, operator error, material defect, software fault). Sourced from the plant's root cause taxonomy maintained in Maximo or the CMMS. Used for CAPA initiation and FMEA updates. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product with full root cause taxonomy]

attributes.name: root_cause_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description of the identified root cause of the downtime event, as entered by the maintenance technician or engineer. Complements the structured root_cause_code with contextual detail for CAPA and FMEA analysis.

attributes.name: safety_incident_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the associated safety incident report when is_safety_incident is True. Links the downtime event to the EHS (Environmental Health and Safety) management system for OSHA compliance reporting.

attributes.name: source_event_reference
attributes.description: The native identifier of this downtime event in the originating source system (e.g., Maximo work order number, Opcenter MES downtime record ID, SCADA alarm ID). Enables traceability back to the system of record for reconciliation and audit.

attributes.name: spare_parts_used
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or free-text description of spare parts consumed during the repair of this downtime event (e.g., part numbers, descriptions). Used for spare parts consumption tracking, inventory replenishment, and maintenance cost analysis. Detailed parts data is managed in Maximo inventory.

attributes.name: start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the equipment stoppage began. Principal real-world event timestamp for the downtime event. Captured from SCADA/MES automated detection or manual operator entry. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: technician_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for maintenance technician observations, diagnostic findings, and repair actions taken during the downtime event. Captured in Maximo work order long description. Supports knowledge management and future FMEA updates.

products.name: spare_part
products.description: Spare parts and MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Operations) materials master record specific to asset maintenance, including part number, description, manufacturer part number, OEM compatibility list (linked to equipment classes and specific assets), criticality classification (insurance spares, critical, non-critical), ABC classification for inventory prioritization, reorder point, safety stock level, lead time, unit of measure, storeroom bin location, interchangeability/supersession chain, and shelf life expiry where applicable. Distinct from production inventory — focused on maintenance-specific materials managed in Maximo Inventory and SAP MM-PM integration. Serves as the SSOT for maintenance material identity and stocking parameters.
products.reference: Maximo Item Master / SAP MM Material Master (MRO)

attributes.name: spare_part_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated surrogate identifier for the spare part master record in the Maximo Inventory and SAP MM-PM integration. Serves as the primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to engineering.component. Business justification: Spare‑part inventory matches parts to engineering component definitions for correct replacement and cost estimation.

attributes.name: drawing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to engineering.drawing. Business justification: Spare parts are identified and procured using engineering drawings. drawing_number on spare_part is a denormalized reference to engineering.drawing. Linking enables direct drawing retrieval for mainte

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_location. Business justification: Spare parts are stored at a physical location; linking to asset_location eliminates redundant location fields and enables location‑based inventory queries.

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.material_master. Business justification: MRO procurement, stock valuation, and replenishment planning require every spare part to be linked to its material master record. Enables spare part reorder point management, ABC classification alignm

attributes.name: procurement_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.procurement_contract. Business justification: Spare parts procured under blanket/framework contracts require contract linkage for correct pricing, compliance reporting, and release-order management. MRO contract compliance is a standard manufactu

attributes.name: purchase_info_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_info_record. Business justification: Spare parts sourcing relies on purchase info records for preferred vendor, price, and lead time. Maintenance planners use PIRs when ordering MRO materials. Replaces denormalized preferred_vendor_numbe

attributes.name: sku_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.sku_master. Business justification: Enables inventory, procurement and cost tracking by linking each spare part to its SKU definition used in MRP and purchasing.

attributes.name: stock_location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to inventory.stock_location. Business justification: Spare‑part inventory management uses stock_location to locate bins; linking enables accurate stock counts, replenishment planning, and pick‑list generation.

attributes.name: abc_class
attributes.description: ABC classification for inventory prioritization based on annual consumption value. 'A' items represent high-value, high-priority parts requiring tight inventory control; 'B' items are moderate value; 'C' items are low-value, high-volume parts with relaxed control. Aligns with SAP MM ABC Indicator and supports MRP/MRP II planning.

attributes.name: average_annual_consumption
attributes.description: Average quantity of this spare part consumed per year across all work orders and maintenance activities. Used for ABC classification, reorder point calculation, and inventory optimization in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management.

attributes.name: capex_asset_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this spare part is classified as a capital expenditure (CapEx) item that must be capitalized on the asset register rather than expensed as operational expenditure (OpEx). Drives financial treatment in SAP FI/CO and supports CapEx asset register management.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the spare part master record was first created in the source system (Maximo or SAP MM). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and record lifecycle tracking per ISO 9001 document control requirements.

attributes.name: criticality_class
attributes.description: Maintenance criticality classification of the spare part. 'insurance_spare' denotes a high-value, long-lead-time part held solely to protect against catastrophic equipment failure; 'critical' denotes parts whose absence would cause significant production downtime; 'non_critical' denotes parts with readily available substitutes or low downtime impact. Drives stocking policy and capital allocation decisions.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the standard cost and last purchase price fields (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Enables multi-currency reporting across global manufacturing plants.

attributes.name: hazardous_material_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this spare part is classified as a hazardous material requiring special handling, storage, or disposal procedures under OSHA or EPA regulations. Drives safety data sheet (SDS) requirements and storeroom segregation rules.

attributes.name: hazmat_class_code
attributes.description: Regulatory hazardous material classification code (e.g., UN/DOT hazard class) for spare parts flagged as hazardous. Required for compliant storage, transport documentation, and EPA/OSHA reporting. Null when hazardous_material_flag is false.

attributes.name: interchangeable_part_numbers
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of alternative part numbers that are functionally interchangeable with this spare part. Supports maintenance technician substitution decisions when the primary part is out of stock. Managed in Maximo Item Cross-Reference.

attributes.name: last_issued_date
attributes.description: Date on which this spare part was most recently issued from the storeroom to a maintenance work order. Used to identify slow-moving or dormant inventory for stock rationalization and obsolescence review.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the spare part master record was most recently updated in the source system. Used for change tracking, delta load processing in the Databricks Silver Layer, and audit compliance.

attributes.name: last_purchase_price
attributes.description: Most recent purchase price per unit of measure paid to a supplier for this spare part. Sourced from SAP MM purchasing info record (EINA/EINE) or Maximo PO history. Used for budget estimation and procurement benchmarking.

attributes.name: last_received_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent goods receipt was posted for this spare part in the storeroom. Used to track replenishment activity and assess supplier delivery performance.

attributes.name: maintenance_strategy
attributes.description: Maintenance strategy associated with this spare part, indicating the primary maintenance approach for which the part is consumed. Supports Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) planning and work order scheduling in Maximo and SAP PM.

attributes.name: material_group_code
attributes.description: SAP Material Group (MATKL) code classifying the spare part into a procurement category for spend analysis, sourcing strategy, and reporting. Aligns with SAP Ariba category management and supports CapEx/OpEx classification.

attributes.name: max_stock_qty
attributes.description: Maximum allowable on-hand inventory quantity for this spare part in the storeroom. Used to prevent overstocking and manage storeroom space. Corresponds to SAP MM Maximum Stock Level (MABST) and Maximo Maximum Quantity.

attributes.name: minimum_order_qty
attributes.description: Minimum quantity that must be ordered per purchase order line for this spare part, as stipulated by the supplier or procurement policy. Corresponds to SAP MM Minimum Order Quantity (MINBE) and Maximo Order Unit.

attributes.name: mro_category
attributes.description: MRO procurement category classifying the spare part within the broader maintenance materials taxonomy. Used for spend analytics, category management in SAP Ariba, and OpEx reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spare_parts|consumables|lubricants|tools|safety_supplies|electrical_supplies — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: part_description
attributes.description: Long-form technical description of the spare part including functional purpose, specifications, and application context. Supports maintenance technician identification and procurement sourcing.

attributes.name: part_name
attributes.description: Short descriptive name of the spare part as used in maintenance work orders, purchase requisitions, and storeroom pick lists. Corresponds to SAP Material Short Text (MAKTX) and Maximo Item Description.

attributes.name: part_number
attributes.description: The internal part number (material number) assigned to the spare part in SAP MM / Maximo Inventory. This is the primary business identifier used across procurement, maintenance work orders, and storeroom operations. Corresponds to SAP Material Number (MATNR) and Maximo Item Number.

attributes.name: part_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the spare part master record. 'active' indicates the part is in use and available for procurement and work orders; 'obsolete' indicates the part is no longer supported; 'superseded' indicates it has been replaced by another part number; 'pending_approval' indicates the record is under review; 'blocked' indicates procurement or usage is temporarily suspended.

attributes.name: part_type
attributes.description: Technical classification of the spare part by engineering discipline. Drives routing to the correct maintenance trade, storeroom zone, and procurement category. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mechanical|electrical|electronic|hydraulic|pneumatic|consumable|structural|instrumentation — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: procurement_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the spare part is procured externally from a supplier ('external'), produced internally ('internal'), or both. Corresponds to SAP MM Procurement Type (BESKZ) and drives MRP planning logic.

attributes.name: quality_inspection_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this spare part requires a quality inspection upon goods receipt before it can be issued to a work order. Corresponds to SAP QM Inspection Type 01 (Goods Receipt Inspection) and supports ISO 9001 incoming quality control requirements.

attributes.name: reorder_point
attributes.description: Inventory level at which a replenishment order is automatically triggered in SAP MRP or Maximo Inventory. Calculated based on average consumption rate, lead time, and safety stock. Expressed in the part's base unit of measure.

attributes.name: replenishment_lead_time_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days from purchase order placement to receipt of the spare part at the storeroom. Used in reorder point calculation and MRP planning. Corresponds to SAP MM Planned Delivery Time (PLIFZ) and Maximo Lead Time.

attributes.name: safety_stock_qty
attributes.description: Minimum buffer stock quantity maintained to protect against demand variability and supply lead time uncertainty. Corresponds to SAP MM Safety Stock (EISBE) and Maximo Safety Stock field. Expressed in the part's base unit of measure.

attributes.name: shelf_life_days
attributes.description: Maximum number of days this spare part can be stored before it expires or degrades below acceptable quality standards. Applicable to consumables, lubricants, seals, gaskets, and chemical materials. Corresponds to SAP MM Total Shelf Life (MHDRZ). Zero or null indicates no shelf life restriction.

attributes.name: standard_cost
attributes.description: Standard cost per unit of measure for the spare part as maintained in SAP MM valuation (moving average or standard price). Used for inventory valuation, work order cost accounting, and CapEx/OpEx reporting. Expressed in the plant's local currency.

attributes.name: superseded_by_part_number
attributes.description: Part number of the replacement spare part that supersedes this record in the interchangeability/supersession chain. Populated when part_status is 'superseded'. Enables maintenance planners to identify the correct current part for work orders.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Base unit of measure for the spare part as defined in SAP MM (MEINS) and Maximo. Governs how the part is stocked, issued, and ordered. Common values include EA (each), KG (kilogram), L (litre), M (metre), SET, BOX. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|KG|L|M|M2|M3|SET|BOX|ROLL|PAIR — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: valuation_class
attributes.description: SAP MM Valuation Class (BKLAS) that determines the general ledger (GL) accounts posted when inventory movements occur for this spare part. Critical for financial integration between MM and FI/CO modules.

attributes.name: warranty_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the manufacturer's warranty for this spare part expires. Used to trigger warranty claims before expiry and to avoid unnecessary procurement of parts still under warranty coverage.

attributes.name: weight_kg
attributes.description: Gross weight of the spare part per base unit of measure, expressed in kilograms. Used for logistics planning, freight cost estimation, and storeroom load calculations. Corresponds to SAP MM Gross Weight (BRGEW).

products.name: calibration_record
products.description: Instrument and measurement equipment calibration record tracking calibration events for gauges, sensors, PLCs, and precision measurement tools. Captures calibration date, calibration standard used, as-found reading, as-left reading, tolerance limits, pass/fail result, calibration interval, next due date, and certifying technician. Supports ISO 9001 measurement system compliance and SPC instrument traceability.

attributes.name: calibration_record_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each calibration record event. Primary key for the calibration_record data product.

attributes.name: asset_work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Maximo work order under which this calibration activity was planned and executed. Enables traceability from calibration event back to maintenance scheduling.

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: Calibration records for customer-owned instruments or customer-dedicated production equipment must be traceable to the customer account for regulatory compliance reporting (ISO, FDA) and customer audi

attributes.name: engineering_specification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to engineering.engineering_specification. Business justification: Calibration records must reference the engineering specification defining the instrument's tolerance limits, calibration method, and acceptance criteria. tolerance_lower_limit and tolerance_upper_limi

attributes.name: equipment_register_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical instrument, gauge, sensor, PLC, or precision measurement tool that was calibrated. Links to the asset master record in Maximo Asset Management.

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.description: Reference to the plant, facility, or functional location where the instrument is installed and where the calibration was performed. Supports site-level compliance reporting and geographic traceability.

attributes.name: pm_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_pm_schedule. Business justification: Calibration activities for instruments and measurement equipment are typically scheduled and triggered by preventive maintenance schedules. Adding asset_pm_schedule_id to calibration_record links each

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: External calibration services are procured via purchase orders. Linking calibration records to the commissioning PO supports three-way match, regulatory audit trails (ISO 17025), and external lab cost

attributes.name: shipment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to logistics.shipment. Business justification: ISO 17025 / regulatory compliance: instruments sent to external calibration labs require shipment tracking for chain-of-custody, certificate validity, and audit trails. calibration_record already has

attributes.name: sku_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.sku_master. Business justification: Calibration activities are performed on specific instrument models; linking to SKU provides traceability for compliance and performance reporting.

attributes.name: work_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.work_center. Business justification: ISO 9001 clause 7.1.5 requires traceability of calibrated instruments to their point of use. Calibration records must link to the work center where the instrument is used for quality audit trails and

attributes.name: adjustment_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the adjustment or corrective action applied to the instrument during calibration (e.g., zero offset correction, span adjustment, sensor replacement). Populated only when adjustment_made is True.

attributes.name: adjustment_made
attributes.description: Indicates whether a physical adjustment or correction was applied to the instrument during this calibration event. True if the instrument was adjusted; False if it was verified only. Drives downstream impact assessment for prior measurements.

attributes.name: as_found_error
attributes.description: The calculated deviation of the as-found reading from the reference value (as_found_reading minus reference_value). Stored as a business fact to support drift trend analysis and SPC instrument capability studies without requiring recalculation.

attributes.name: as_found_reading
attributes.description: The measured value of the instrument at the start of the calibration event, before any adjustment is made. Used to assess instrument drift, determine if prior measurements were valid, and support SPC instrument traceability analysis.

attributes.name: as_left_error
attributes.description: The calculated deviation of the as-left reading from the reference value (as_left_reading minus reference_value). Confirms residual error after adjustment and is used for measurement uncertainty budgets.

attributes.name: as_left_reading
attributes.description: The measured value of the instrument at the conclusion of the calibration event, after any adjustment or correction has been applied. Confirms the instrument is within tolerance before being returned to service.

attributes.name: calibration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the calibration activity was physically performed. This is the principal business event date used for certificate issuance, compliance records, and next-due-date calculation.

attributes.name: calibration_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the next calibration must be completed, calculated from calibration_date plus the calibration_interval. Used for preventive maintenance scheduling and compliance monitoring.

attributes.name: calibration_interval_days
attributes.description: The approved recalibration frequency expressed in calendar days. Used to compute calibration_due_date and to schedule preventive maintenance in Maximo. Determined by instrument criticality, historical drift, and manufacturer recommendations.

attributes.name: calibration_lab
attributes.description: Indicates whether the calibration was performed by an internal calibration lab, an externally accredited laboratory (ISO/IEC 17025), an external non-accredited service provider, or the OEM service team.

attributes.name: calibration_method
attributes.description: The documented calibration procedure or method reference used (e.g., internal procedure number, NIST traceable method, manufacturer procedure). Ensures repeatability and traceability of the calibration process.

attributes.name: calibration_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for the technician to record observations, anomalies, special conditions, or additional context about the calibration event not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: calibration_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable unique identifier for this calibration event, used on calibration certificates and quality records. Format: CAL-{ASSET_CODE}-{SEQUENCE}.

attributes.name: calibration_status
attributes.description: Overall result and lifecycle status of the calibration event. 'pass' indicates the instrument is within tolerance; 'fail' triggers quarantine and CAPA; 'conditional_pass' indicates marginal acceptance with restrictions; 'out_of_tolerance' indicates as-found deviation requiring adjustment.

attributes.name: calibration_type
attributes.description: Classification of the calibration event by trigger or purpose. 'initial' is performed on new instruments; 'periodic' is routine scheduled calibration; 'after_repair' follows maintenance; 'unscheduled' is triggered by suspected drift or incident.

attributes.name: capa_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) Reference Number
attributes.description: Reference number of the Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) record initiated as a result of a calibration failure or out-of-tolerance finding. Links the calibration event to the quality management corrective action workflow.

tag_set.value: CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) Reference Number

attributes.name: certificate_issue_date
attributes.description: The date on which the calibration certificate was formally issued and signed. May differ from calibration_date if review and approval occur after the physical calibration activity.

attributes.name: certificate_number
attributes.description: The official certificate number issued upon successful calibration, as printed on the calibration certificate. Used for document control, quality records management, and regulatory audit evidence.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this calibration record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and compliance record retention tracking.

attributes.name: environmental_humidity_pct
attributes.description: Relative humidity percentage recorded at the time and location of calibration. Required environmental condition documentation per ISO/IEC 17025 for humidity-sensitive instruments.

attributes.name: environmental_temperature_c
attributes.description: Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the time and location of calibration. Environmental conditions can affect measurement accuracy and are required to be documented per ISO/IEC 17025.

attributes.name: external_lab_accreditation_number
attributes.description: Accreditation body certificate number for the external calibration laboratory (e.g., A2LA, NVLAP, UKAS accreditation number). Validates the laboratory's ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation status.

attributes.name: external_lab_name
attributes.description: Name of the external calibration service provider or accredited laboratory, when calibration_lab is 'external_accredited' or 'external_non_accredited'. Used for supplier qualification and audit trail.

attributes.name: instrument_tag
attributes.description: Plant or facility tag number assigned to the measurement instrument per ISA-5.1 instrumentation standards (e.g., TI-101, PT-205). Used for shop floor identification and P&ID cross-reference.

attributes.name: instrument_type
attributes.description: Classification of the measurement instrument or device being calibrated. Drives applicable calibration procedures and tolerance standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: gauge|sensor|transducer|transmitter|analyzer|controller|plc|cnc_probe|torque_wrench|caliper|micrometer|thermometer|pressure_meter|flow_meter — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: measurement_parameter
attributes.description: The physical or process parameter being measured by the instrument (e.g., temperature, pressure, flow, voltage, torque, dimension, weight). Determines the applicable calibration standard and tolerance regime.

attributes.name: measurement_uncertainty
attributes.description: The expanded measurement uncertainty (k=2, 95% confidence) associated with the calibration result, expressed in the same unit as measurement_unit. Required for ISO/IEC 17025 accredited calibration certificates.

attributes.name: measurement_unit
attributes.description: The unit of measure applicable to as_found_reading, as_left_reading, reference_value, and tolerance fields (e.g., °C, bar, mA, mm, Nm, V, kg). Must conform to SI units per ISO 80000.

attributes.name: out_of_service
attributes.description: Indicates whether the instrument has been placed out of service as a result of this calibration event (e.g., due to a fail or out-of-tolerance result). When True, the instrument must be quarantined and a CAPA initiated before return to service.

attributes.name: prior_measurement_impact
attributes.description: Assessment of whether measurements taken by this instrument since its last calibration may have been affected by the out-of-tolerance condition found. Required for product conformity risk assessment when a calibration failure is detected.

attributes.name: reference_value
attributes.description: The true or nominal value against which the instrument reading is compared during calibration. Established by the reference standard and used to compute as-found and as-left errors.

attributes.name: standard_certificate_number
attributes.description: Certificate number of the reference standard used during calibration, establishing the NIST/SI traceability chain. Required for ISO/IEC 17025 compliance documentation.

attributes.name: technician_certification_number
attributes.description: The qualification or certification number of the technician who performed the calibration, as issued by an accredited body (e.g., ASQ, NIST, internal competency register). Required for ISO/IEC 17025 personnel traceability.

attributes.name: technician_name
attributes.description: Full name of the qualified technician who performed and certified the calibration. Captured as a denormalized field on the calibration certificate for regulatory traceability even if the technician record changes.

attributes.name: tolerance_lower_limit

products.name: part_applicability
products.description: This association product represents the Part Applicability contract between spare_part and equipment_register. It captures the operational record of which spare parts are applicable to which equipment instances, including the required quantity, criticality classification for that specific equipment, and installation position. Each record links one spare_part to one equipment_register and carries attributes that exist only in the context of this specific equipment-part combination — they cannot reside on either the spare part master or the equipment register alone. This is a first-class business entity actively managed by maintenance planners in Maximo and SAP PM to drive spare parts optimization, min/max stock setting, and critical spare identification.. Existence Justification: In CMMS and EAM systems (Maximo, SAP PM), the Equipment-Spare Part applicability list is a first-class operational business concept known as 'Spare Part Applicability' or 'Equipment BOM for Maintenance'. Maintenance planners actively create, update, and delete these records to define which spare parts are applicable to which equipment, at what quantities, and with what criticality — this is core to spare parts optimization, min/max stock setting, and critical spare identification. The M:N cardinality is unambiguous and operationally real: one spare part applies to many equipment instances (e.g., a bearing used across 12 CNC machines), and one equipment instance requires many spare parts (e.g., a CNC machine requires bearings, belts, filters, seals).

attributes.name: spare_part_id

attributes.references: Maximo Spare Part Applicability criticality field

[Moved from spare_part: Same rationale as equipment_category — this is a class-level proxy for applicability that is superseded by the instance-level part_applicability association. If equipment class applicability is needed, it should be modeled as a separate class-level applicability relationship, not as a denormalized attribute on the spare part master.]

attributes.name: recommended_stock_qty

products.name: job_plan_material_requirement
products.description: This association product represents the Material Requirement contract between a job_plan and a spare_part. It captures the standardized bill of materials for a maintenance procedure — specifically, which spare parts are required, in what quantity, in what sequence, and whether each part is mandatory or optional for executing the job plan. Each record links one job_plan to one spare_part with attributes that exist only in the context of this planned material requirement (quantity, sequence, mandatory flag, estimated cost). This is the structured replacement for the denormalized spare_parts_list string on the job_plan entity, and is the SSOT for maintenance material planning in Maximo Job Plan Material Lists and SAP PM Task Component Lists.. Existence Justification: In CMMS-driven manufacturing environments, a Job Plan (standardized maintenance procedure template) explicitly defines a Bill of Materials — a list of spare parts required to execute that procedure. A single job plan requires multiple spare parts (e.g., bearings, seals, lubricants, gaskets), and a single spare part appears on many job plans (e.g., a common bearing used in pump overhaul, motor replacement, and conveyor maintenance job plans). This is the canonical 'Job Plan Material List' or 'Task Material Requirements' concept in Maximo and SAP PM, actively managed by maintenance planners who create, update, and delete part requirements per job plan.

The line-level estimated_cost now lives on the association; the job_plan aggregate can be computed or retained as a denormalized summary. If retained on job_plan, it should be clearly marked as a derived/computed field, not a source attribute.]

domains.name: inventory

Integrates SAP WM and Microsoft Dynamics 365 SCM for real-time stock visibility and MRP-driven replenishment.

products.name: stock_location
products.description: Master record for all physical storage locations within warehouses and facilities, including bin, rack, shelf, zone, and aisle designations. Captures location type (bulk, pick, reserve, staging), capacity constraints, temperature and environmental requirements, and coordinate-based bin addressing. Serves as the single source of truth for all bin-level location data used for real-time stock placement, retrieval, and directed put-away across all manufacturing facilities.
products.reference: SAP WM Storage Bin / WMS Bin Location

attributes.name: stock_location_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the physical storage location within warehouses and facilities. Primary key for the stock location master record.

attributes.name: consignment_address_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.address. Business justification: In VMI/consignment manufacturing operations, a stock_location physically resides at a customer site. Linking to customer.address enables replenishment logistics, delivery scheduling, and VMI site mana

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: Consignment inventory tracking requires linking each stock location to the owning customer account for ownership and billing.

attributes.name: warehouse_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent warehouse or facility where this storage location resides. Links to the facility master for site-level aggregation and reporting.

attributes.name: abc_classification
attributes.description: ABC classification of the storage location based on inventory velocity and value. A-class locations store high-velocity or high-value items in the most accessible zones. B-class locations store medium-velocity items. C-class locations store slow-moving items in less accessible areas. Used for warehouse slotting optimization and space allocation.

attributes.name: access_equipment_required
attributes.description: Type of material handling equipment required to access this storage location. Determines labor and equipment resource planning for put-away and picking operations. Influences cycle time calculations and warehouse operational efficiency metrics (OEE). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|forklift|reach_truck|order_picker|crane|agv|manual — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: aisle_number
attributes.description: Aisle identifier within the warehouse zone. Aisles are the primary navigation paths for material handlers and automated guided vehicles (AGVs). Used for directed put-away and optimized picking routes.

attributes.name: bin_position
attributes.description: Horizontal bin position within the shelf level. Represents the finest granularity of storage location addressing. Used for precise material placement and retrieval in high-density storage environments.

attributes.name: capacity_pallet_positions
attributes.description: Number of standard pallet positions that can be stored in this location. Used for pallet storage locations to calculate available capacity and optimize warehouse space utilization. Assumes standard pallet dimensions (e.g., 1200mm x 1000mm EUR pallet or 1219mm x 1016mm North American pallet).

attributes.name: capacity_volume_m3
attributes.description: Maximum volumetric capacity of the storage location measured in cubic meters. Used for space utilization analysis, slotting optimization, and warehouse capacity planning. Constrains the physical size of materials that can be stored in this location.

attributes.name: capacity_weight_kg
attributes.description: Maximum weight capacity of the storage location measured in kilograms. Enforces structural load limits for racks and shelves. Critical for safety compliance and preventing equipment damage. Used in slotting algorithms to match heavy materials with appropriate locations.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Date when this storage location record was initially created in the warehouse management system. Used for master data audit trails, location lifecycle tracking, and warehouse expansion analysis.

attributes.name: cycle_count_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which this storage location is scheduled for cycle counting inventory verification. High-value or high-velocity locations typically have higher cycle count frequencies. Used to generate cycle count schedules and ensure inventory accuracy per ISO 9001 quality management requirements.

attributes.name: deactivation_date
attributes.description: Date when this storage location was deactivated or retired from operational use. Deactivated locations are no longer available for material placement but may retain historical inventory transaction data. Used for warehouse reconfiguration tracking and capacity planning analysis.

attributes.name: fifo_enforced
attributes.business_glossary_term: First In First Out (FIFO) Enforced Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this location enforces First In First Out (FIFO) inventory rotation. FIFO ensures older materials are consumed before newer materials, critical for perishable goods, time-sensitive components, and materials with shelf-life constraints. Used by warehouse management systems (WMS) to generate FIFO-compliant pick instructions.

tag_set.value: First In First Out (FIFO) Enforced Flag

attributes.name: fire_zone
attributes.description: Fire safety zone identifier for this storage location. Fire zones group locations by fire suppression system coverage and emergency response protocols. Critical for safety compliance, emergency planning, and hazardous material segregation per OSHA and NFPA standards.

attributes.name: humidity_controlled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this location maintains controlled humidity levels. Humidity control is critical for materials susceptible to moisture damage, corrosion, or degradation such as electronics, metal components, and hygroscopic materials.

attributes.name: humidity_max_percent
attributes.description: Maximum allowable relative humidity percentage for this storage location. Enforces upper humidity boundary to prevent condensation, corrosion, or mold growth. Typically ranges from 50% to 70% for general storage, lower for electronics.

attributes.name: humidity_min_percent
attributes.description: Minimum allowable relative humidity percentage for this storage location. Enforces lower humidity boundary to prevent static electricity buildup or material desiccation. Typically ranges from 20% to 40% for electronics and sensitive components.

attributes.name: is_hazmat_approved
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this location is certified and approved for storing hazardous materials. Hazmat-approved locations must meet specific safety, ventilation, containment, and regulatory requirements per OSHA and EPA standards. Used to enforce material placement rules for dangerous goods.

attributes.name: is_picking_location
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this location is designated as a primary picking location for order fulfillment. Picking locations are typically positioned in ergonomic zones with high accessibility and are replenished from reserve locations. Used by warehouse management systems (WMS) to optimize pick path generation.

attributes.name: is_replenishment_location
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this location serves as a reserve or bulk storage location that feeds picking locations through replenishment processes. Replenishment locations typically have higher capacity and lower accessibility than picking locations.

attributes.name: last_cycle_count_date
attributes.description: Date when the most recent cycle count was performed for this storage location. Used to track cycle count compliance, identify overdue counts, and calculate inventory accuracy metrics. Critical for maintaining inventory integrity and meeting audit requirements.

attributes.name: location_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code identifying the storage location within the warehouse. Used for barcode scanning, pick lists, and warehouse management system (WMS) transactions. Typically follows a structured format combining zone, aisle, rack, shelf, and bin identifiers.

attributes.name: location_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name for the storage location. Provides business context beyond the technical location code for reporting and user interfaces.

attributes.name: location_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the storage location. Active locations are available for material placement and retrieval. Blocked locations are temporarily unavailable due to quality holds, damage, or operational restrictions. Maintenance status indicates the location is undergoing repair or inspection. Reserved status indicates the location is allocated for specific materials or operations. Full status indicates the location has reached capacity.

attributes.name: location_type
attributes.description: Classification of the storage location based on its operational purpose within the warehouse. Bulk locations store large quantities, pick locations support order fulfillment, reserve locations hold overflow inventory, staging areas facilitate material movement, quarantine zones isolate non-conforming materials, and cross-dock areas enable direct transfer without storage. attributes.name: mixed_sku_allowed

attributes.name: rack_number

attributes.name: temperature_controlled

attributes.name: temperature_min_c

attributes.name: x_coordinate

attributes.name: y_coordinate

attributes.name: z_coordinate

attributes.name: zone_code
attributes.description: High-level zone identifier within the warehouse (e.g., A, B, C or NORTH, SOUTH). Zones group locations by physical area, product category, or operational function to optimize picking routes and material flow.

attributes.description: Classification of hazardous material type per UN/DOT regulations. Examples: flammable liquid, corrosive, toxic, oxidizer. Determines packaging, labeling, and shipping requirements.

attributes.name: hazardous_material_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the material is classified as hazardous. Triggers additional safety, handling, storage, and transportation requirements per OSHA and EPA regulations.

attributes.name: height
attributes.description: Height dimension of the material. Used for storage bin assignment, handling equipment selection, and transportation planning.

attributes.name: inspection_setup_indicator

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.business_glossary_term: Material Master Last Modified By User
attributes.description: User ID of the person who last modified the material master record. Used for audit trail and data governance.

tag_set.value: Material Master Last Modified By User

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Date when the material master record was last changed. Used for audit trail and change management tracking.

attributes.name: length
attributes.description: Length dimension of the material. Used for storage bin assignment, handling equipment selection, and transportation planning.

attributes.name: lot_size
attributes.description: Lot-sizing procedure code determining how procurement or production quantities are calculated. Examples: EX (exact order quantity), FX (fixed lot size), HB (lot-for-lot).

attributes.name: manufacturer_name
attributes.description: Name of the original manufacturer or OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) of the material. Used for quality tracking, warranty claims, and supplier management.

attributes.name: manufacturer_part_number
attributes.description: Original part number assigned by the manufacturer or OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer). Used for cross-referencing, procurement, and technical documentation.

attributes.name: material_description
attributes.description: Full textual description of the material including key characteristics, specifications, and usage. Used for identification and communication across procurement, production, and sales.

attributes.name: material_group
attributes.description: Hierarchical classification code grouping materials with similar characteristics for procurement, planning, and reporting purposes. Used in MRP (Material Requirements Planning) and purchasing strategies.

attributes.name: material_number
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the material assigned by the enterprise. This is the externally-known SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) code used across all systems and documentation.

attributes.name: material_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the material master record. Controls whether the material can be procured, produced, or sold. Blocked materials cannot be used in new transactions.

attributes.name: material_type
attributes.description: Classification of the material based on its role in the manufacturing and supply chain process. Determines procurement, production, and inventory management rules.
